A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LOOP research. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The implementation details and qualitative examples in v1's appendices are retained in v5's main document.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion fine-tuning results, including benchmark scores, repeated-run training curves, a training-variance analysis and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v5 retains original fine-tuning results in Tables 1–3, training curves in Figures 2–3 and qualitative image comparisons.

M1.justification: The LOOP objective and leave-one-out baseline are unchanged: v1 Equations 14 and 16 correspond to v5 Equations 13 and 14. Both combine multiple trajectories with importance sampling, clipping and baseline correction. The new GRPO discussion explains existing formulation choices rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate color, shape, texture, spatial relationships and numeracy, alongside aesthetics and image-text alignment. Although v5 removes the numeracy training-curve panel, numeracy remains evaluated in Table 2.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain the same REINFORCE variants and compositionality baselines. PPO attributed to Black et al. in v1 is explicitly identified as DDPO in v5, rather than replaced by another comparator. GRPO is discussed but expressly not evaluated.

E3.justification: Both retain Stable Diffusion v2 with full UNet fine-tuning, the same reported hyperparameters and hardware settings, and reward averaging over 10 generated images per held-out prompt. No revision to splits, metrics or training budgets is reported; v1 Appendix A is moved to v5 Section 6.

E4.justification: v5 removes the entire 'Impact on training variance' analysis and v1 Figure 4, eliminating the direct empirical examination of variance reduction on color and aesthetics. It also removes the k=2 compositionality validation row, although other k-sensitivity evidence remains. Section 4 adds an unquantified statement that KL-penalty experiments provided little benefit.

E5.justification: The retained training curves in Figures 2–3 still report averages over three runs with 80% prediction intervals. No changed seed information, repeated-run counts, significance testing or uncertainty-reporting procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Retained table scores match, but v5 omits v1's LOOP(k=2) compositionality row, numeracy training curves and training-variance results. Section 7.2 changes the image-alignment improvement from 2.16% to 2.4%, although the unchanged Table 3 values, 20.466 and 20.909, imply approximately 2.16%.

T1.justification: v5 removes Proposition 4.1 and its proof asserting that LOOP's estimator variance equals PPO's variance divided by K squared. This eliminates the method-specific formal variance guarantee, while Theorem 3.1 remains. v5 also explicitly identifies the bias introduced by a baseline averaging rewards including the current sample.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain the same substantive claims: characterize the REINFORCE–PPO trade-off, introduce LOOP's combined approach, and demonstrate improved diffusion fine-tuning. The expanded conclusion restates these claims and existing performance comparisons.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations for omitting reward normalization, KL regularization and generation-length normalization, and acknowledges the absence of a GRPO comparison. It expands interpretation of existing qualitative images and removes the interpretation that the variance experiment validates LOOP's mechanism. The increased training-cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix A and v5 Section 6 provide the same denoising steps, guidance weight, AdamW settings, gradient clipping, eight A100 GPUs, batch size and PPO clipping parameter. Moving this information into the main text adds no implementation settings or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v5 substantially revises positioning against the closely related GRPO approach, describing technical distinctions, claiming independent development and acknowledging no direct comparison. It adds Shao et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2025) and Shenfeld et al. (2025) to support this discussion; v1 positions LOOP principally through PPO and RLOO.

P1.justification: v5 incorporates the appendices into main-text implementation and qualitative sections, adds GRPO discussions and a document roadmap, and substantially expands the conclusion and qualitative narrative. PPO/DDPO terminology is clarified, while much of the background remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, with extensive table and figure relocation. Tables 1–2 exchange order, Figure 3 changes from seven panels to six, and the variance figure disappears. The existing appendix image grids become Figures 4–5 in the main document.

improvement.justification: v5 improves positioning through the GRPO discussion and removes a variance proof whose K-squared scaling does not follow from the stated independence assumption. However, it also removes direct variance-analysis evidence and some k=2 results while retaining variance-reduction claims, and introduces the incorrect 2.4% alignment-gain statement. The gains in precision and contextualization coexist with reduced empirical support and a numerical inconsistency, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
